title: Compact toolchain loader and presubmit throttle
author: Liam O'Connor
release_notes: Reduce presubmit runner image size and speed up fast-path CI by adding a compact toolchain loader and configurable presubmit throttling. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: Presubmit runners are a major contributor to CI latency and developer feedback time. Our monolithic toolchain images pull ~1.2GB and start multiple auxiliary services on every job. For nightly/integration flows this is acceptable, but the fast-path presubmit experience (lint, unit, smoke) needs faster startup and lighter disk/IO pressure. This change introduces a compact toolchain loader (lazy bootstrap of heavy components) and a presubmit throttle layer that samples heavy integration tests for long-running PRs to improve median feedback time without reducing coverage in nightly jobs.

What this PR does (single-string summary): - Adds a compact toolchain loader binary (cmd/ctloader) that prepares minimal runtime for fast-path jobs and lazily fetches/initializes heavy components (language toolchains, optional test daemons) only when requested. - Introduces a presubmit-throttle action step for GitHub Actions that can be enabled per-path or per-branch to sample heavy tests at a configurable rate. - Reworks Dockerfiles and build scripts to produce a second, slim toolchain image (toolchain:slim) and changes CI matrices to use it for fast lanes. - Adds health-checking and a debug switch to force full bootstrap for debugging flakiness. - Adds lightweight telemetry and a small perf harness to measure startup time in the CI pipeline.

Checklist: [x] compact loader binary + tests, [x] slim Dockerfile and build rules, [x] GitHub Actions presubmit-throttle step + docs, [x] telemetry hooks and dashboard link, [x] updated dev docs and migration note, [x] manual smoke run in staging, [x] CI green after lint fixup.

Backward compatibility / risk: Fast-path jobs will opt-in to the slim image via the new workflow matrix entries. No changes to customer-facing APIs. The only risk is transient test ordering differences when the lazy loader defers initialization; to mitigate, we added a debug env (CTLOADER_FORCE_BOOTSTRAP=1) and smoke checks.

Files changed (high level): - cmd/ctloader/*: compact loader implementation and unit tests - docker/toolchain-slim.Dockerfile: new slim image recipe - .github/workflows/presubmit.yml: added throttle steps and matrix tweak - infra/ci/scripts/bootstrap.sh: refactor split paths, new lazy-fetch hooks - tools/ci/telemetry/ctloader-metrics: perf probe and dashboard config - docs/dev/ci.md: instructions for using slim image and forcing full bootstrap - Makefile: new targets build-slim/push-slim

Summary of commits: commit 1: add compact loader skeleton and CLI flags; commit 2: implement lazy-fetch for language runtimes and KV; commit 3: slim Dockerfile + build targets; commit 4: presubmit-throttle GH Action step and docs; commit 5: fix linting and add unit tests for loader; commit 6: add telemetry probe and dashboard wiring; commit 7: address review comments and add smoke-run orchestration.

Why this is different from previous "slim" attempts: earlier PRs trimmed layers but still required full runtime init; this approach defers expensive init until a job requests it and provides a small, deterministic fast-path for common presubmit checks. It pairs a CI-level throttle so heavy tests are still run at scale but only sampled during rapid feedback.

Operational notes: - toolchain:slim is published to our internal registry under redwood/toolchain:slim-20260202. - Presubmit-throttle defaults to sampling 25% of PRs for heavy integration tests; can be configured via .github/presubmit-config.yaml. - Dashboard: CI -> Presubmit -> Compact Loader (link: https://observability.internal/redwood/ctloader).

Metrics observed in staging (after smoke run): - Slim image pull size: 420MB (was ~1.2GB) - Median presubmit job wall time (fast-path): 3.5m (was 8.0m) - Cold-start time for loader: 4.2s to first-ready, heavy init deferred until 90–120s only when requested.

Migration: update local Makefile targets: make build-slim and CI maintainers should adjust workflow matrices if they want to opt-out of sampling for specific repos.

Related: ENG-1421 (fast presubmit program), ENG-1589 (ci toolchain hygiene).
